title: The River Remembers
visual_narrative: A traveller rests an open journal on a ghat step. One river edge flows out of its page as translucent ink, becoming a real river behind the person; the face, hand and nearest stone remain photographic. The transition follows a curved shoreline, never a straight split.
references: One clear adult portrait; optional owned river/location photograph. No requirement to upload handwriting or private journal pages.
preserve: One recognizable face and actual proportions; keep the photographic face outside the painted region.
transform: Environment edges and blank journal artwork into flowing ink; adapt practical clothing and a quiet glance.
preview_brief: One fictional Indian woman about 42, deep-brown complexion, short wavy hair, ordinary build, in an indigo cotton shirt; copper river light, cream paper and one indigo ink channel. Three-quarter framing, face large and unobscured.
why_ai: Turns a personal travel photograph into a physical-looking memory artwork that requires compositing, illustration and perspective matching.
originality: Continuous river-led transition and a single face, unlike the references' stacked repeated-scene pages; no copied captions.
risks: Ink must not cross facial landmarks or imply the person is dissolving; avoid tiny journal detail as the only hook.
reuse: Could develop the generic island or Paris travel memory, but the new river narrative warrants its own detail record; no existing image proves the effect.
reel_potential: A restrained ink-edge reveal could work after a still succeeds; not selected for initial motion production.
benefit: Turns a personal travel photograph into a physical-looking memory artwork that requires compositing, illustration and perspective matching.

title: One Day, Four Possible Worlds
visual_narrative: One dominant portrait occupies the left two-thirds. Three unequal inset windows show the same adult as a night-sky observer, pottery maker and mountain traveller. Windows share one curved horizon, not a rigid passport grid. Expressions and wardrobe vary; age does not.
references: A clear frontal and optional three-quarter portrait of one adult. One identity, four intentional depictions. Choose pursuits rather than claim real accomplishments.
preserve: Same recognizable face, age, hairline and physique in all four depictions.
transform: Environment, practical wardrobe and expression per pursuit; changes do not imply different ethnic identities.
preview_brief: A fictional Indian man about 35 with medium-brown skin, naturally curly medium-length hair and an ordinary stocky build. Ochre pottery dominant panel, midnight observatory and muted mountain inserts; avoid four identical smiles.
why_ai: Offers four coherent imagined lives from one reference without organising four shoots.
originality: Asymmetric narrative windows and chosen pursuits, not a source character costume, numbered pose sheet or nine warehouse angles.
risks: High identity drift and tiny faces; trial one panel first, then assemble controlled panels. Do not crop this layout to 4:5.
reuse: Reuse persona policy concepts; no final asset available.
reel_potential: Possible later scene sequence with independent reference-conditioned shots; not a morphing transition.
benefit: Offers four coherent imagined lives from one reference without organising four shoots.

title: A Mountain Journey Within
visual_narrative: An almost frontal portrait remains clear from eyes to mouth. A Himalayan road runs through the jacket and outer shoulder silhouette, with a tiny unoccupied roadside tent. A pale sky separates the facial edge from the mountain layers; no second human silhouette.
references: One clear head-and-shoulders portrait; optional owned landscape. One identity and one depiction.
preserve: Eyes, nose, mouth, face geometry and hairline in a photographic neutral-lit zone.
transform: Jacket/shoulder area into a layered mountain landscape; literal colour retained on face, scenery permitted only outside it.
preview_brief: One fictional Indian adult about 58 with light-brown complexion, grey moustache and short salt-and-pepper hair, weatherproof dark jacket; slate mountains and a warm winding road. No implied real expedition achievement.
why_ai: Creates a controlled portrait-landscape composite that would require specialist masking and art direction.
originality: The user's candidate direction is developed into a shoulder-only journey; the inspected sources do not establish a double-exposure example, so this is not claimed as a research finding.
risks: Road crossing the eyes, hollow-looking face or unwanted extra person; keep the face zone explicit.
reuse: Existing mountain scenes can inform setting but are not authorized landscape source plates for a real reference composite.
reel_potential: Gentle environment motion possible later; keep face stable rather than animating an empty silhouette.
benefit: Creates a controlled portrait-landscape composite that would require specialist masking and art direction.

title: Our Courtyard, Small Enough to Hold
visual_narrative: A handcrafted shallow courtyard model sits on a wide wooden shelf. Three family members gather around a tiny chessboard near its front edge, large enough for readable faces. Rear balconies recede in painted card and carved wood; visible glue seams and scale make it a handmade memory rather than a normal house photograph.
references: All family members independently labelled; optional owned home photo. Adapt composition to actual family count, not the fictional sample's three.
preserve: Each person's age, recognizable landmarks and relative body proportions; distinguish identity count from miniature scale.
transform: Uniform scale and surrounding building material; faces remain carefully rendered rather than blank figurines.
preview_brief: Three fictional Indian family members: older woman around 68 with grey braid and deep-brown complexion, adult around 36 with short hair and medium complexion, child around 9 with wavy hair and light-brown complexion. Everyday cotton clothes; warm plaster, teal balcony and terracotta tile.
why_ai: Makes a family/home memory into a photographed bespoke architectural keepsake without commissioning a modelmaker.
originality: A front-edge chess gathering in a shallow courtyard differs from the source street truck diorama and enamel mountain badge.
risks: Small faces and model-like skin reduce recognizability; use a shallow set and only the supplied count. If fidelity fails, frame as a scene keepsake rather than a verified identity result.
reuse: Existing family photos provide no automatic public reference permission; use a new fictional identity fixture. Reuse no final image.
reel_potential: A small move past a wooden column can reveal the family and model edge; R02 candidate.
benefit: Makes a family/home memory into a photographed bespoke architectural keepsake without commissioning a modelmaker.

title: The Last Train, Printed in Two Inks
visual_narrative: A readable close portrait is crossed only at the shoulder by the shadow of a diagonal carriage window. references: One clear portrait; expression and period collar are optional styling choices.
preserve: Recognizable facial geometry, apparent age, hairline and distinguishing marks through tonal relationships.
transform: Entire image into a declared two-ink artwork; ink colour does not claim literal skin colour or altered ethnicity.
preview_brief: Fictional Indian woman around 52, medium-brown complexion, silver-streaked short curls and a broad natural face; saffron/plum print on off-white stock, one diagonal window shadow, plain period blouse.
why_ai: Creates bespoke printable portrait art with controlled material and graphic structure.
originality: Train-window light, two chosen inks and close facial hierarchy replace the source cafe composition and blue/orange palette.
risks: Halftone can erase marks or smooth age; sample at card size and full resolution. Never append a conflicting photorealistic-skin clause.
reuse: Existing photo persona contract requires an art-aware extension; no suitable final asset.
reel_potential: Ink registration reveal is motion graphics rather than live footage; label accordingly if ever used.
benefit: Creates bespoke printable portrait art with controlled material and graphic structure.

title: The Letter Before the Train Leaves
visual_narrative: Develop the existing original concept: two adults exchange one folded letter beside a stationary 1970s-inspired carriage. A sliver of warm station light separates their hands; steam hides the far end of the platform, not their faces. The recipient's smile provides the emotional answer.
references: Two separately identifiable adults or one clear couple reference. Preserve their actual ages; period is wardrobe/set styling only.
preserve: Both identities, complexion, face shape and proportions; any meaningful reference marks.
transform: Period travel clothes, hair arrangement, carriage and steam lighting without copying a film or actor.
preview_brief: Two fictional Indian adults around 45 and 49 with distinct faces and ordinary builds; one with deep-brown skin and loose short curls, one with medium complexion and a greying moustache. Muted maroon and cream travel clothes, amber lamps and cool steam.
why_ai: Creates an emotionally specific period film set with controlled steam, carriage access and lighting.
originality: This is a retained PicMagic original, not a copied rainy-platform poster. Letter hand-off and face reaction differ from back-facing waiting figures and printed layout.
risks: Hand transfer and tiny letter can confuse; still keyframe should show letter already supported between two separate hands.
reuse: Reuse local prompt ID and canonical; old terrace-letter asset lacks carriage/steam and cannot serve as finished preview.
reel_potential: R01: letter edge → hand-off/reaction → warm carriage reveal.
benefit: Creates an emotionally specific period film set with controlled steam, carriage access and lighting.

transform: Weather, lighting, coat and waiting pose, plus a fictional station setting.

why_ai: Builds a narrative rain set with precise lighting and vehicle continuity that is expensive to stage.
originality: The emotional question is a departure decision; no royal-car pose or source platform layout.
risks: Extra driver, door geometry and confusing wet reflections; high vehicle-reference burden.
reuse: Could become a future creative variant of neon-monsoon-drive; do not create both unchanged versions.
reel_potential: Door light → traveller's pause → bag placed safely inside; defer until vehicle geometry is reliable.
benefit: Builds a narrative rain set with precise lighting and vehicle continuity that is expensive to stage.

benefit: Makes a person's craft into an impossible full-scale world without miniature fabrication or giant props.
